title: SSC CGL: response-sheet score, objections and the Tier 2 bridge
description: Learn how to audit a CGL response sheet, calculate raw marks, prepare an evidence-based objection and keep Tier 2 study moving.
intro: The CGL 2026 Tier 1 tentative key and responses are available under SSC’s 4 November notice. Save them before 7 November at 9 PM IST; online challenges cost ₹50 per question/answer. Use this guide to audit raw marks and build the next-stage study plan.

sections.title: Save the key before 7 November at 9 PM
sections.body:
Sign in on [SSC](https://ssc.gov.in/) with your registration number and password. The [4 November notice](https://ssc.gov.in/api/attachment/uploads/masterData/NoticeBoards/writeup_04112026.pdf) opens online challenges from 4 November at 9 PM to 7 November at 9 PM, at ₹50 per question/answer challenged. It says the response sheet and tentative key will not be accessible after this period. Save them for personal use and self-analysis, along with any submission acknowledgement.

The challenge module can show a different order of questions and options from the exam display. Match the actual question, options and selected answer before objecting. The notice records CBT held 30 September–28 October; a tentative-key release does not declare qualification or a Tier 2 date.

sections.title: Save the evidence before calculating
sections.body:
Open the key link through SSC and confirm the exam year, tier, date and shift. Save the question paper with recorded responses and the published key while the official window is available. A coaching answer list is not a substitute for the recorded response SSC uses.

Keep one untouched copy and work on a second copy. Build a small ledger: question ID, recorded choice, official answer, your objection reason and evidence. Question IDs matter more than a screenshot's question number, because display order can differ. Check the deadline and fee in the current notice; an older cycle's window is not permission to submit now.

sections.title: Calculate raw marks with a clear audit trail
sections.body:
For the standard Tier 1 marking of +2 and −0.5, raw marks are **2 × correct − 0.5 × wrong**. Unanswered questions contribute zero. If you attempted 80 and 68 are correct, 12 are wrong: 136 − 6 = 130. Reconcile correct + wrong + unanswered with the total paper before trusting the number.

Use the [CGL score calculator](/exams/ssc-cgl/score-calculator/) as a second check. Raw marks, normalised marks, percentile and rank are different quantities. None can be converted exactly into another from just your response sheet. A revised key or a notice about dropped questions can also alter the calculation.

sections.title: Challenge the answer, not your disappointment
sections.body:
A useful objection identifies the exact question and explains a testable error: an unsupported official option, two valid options, a missing condition or a calculation that contradicts the key. Attach a credible reference with the relevant page or passage when the portal permits it. A social-media poll is weak evidence.

For a maths objection, show the setup and substitution, not only the final value. For language or general awareness, check the wording and date of the source. Submit only through the official tracker and retain the acknowledgement. Paying a challenge fee does not guarantee acceptance; wait for the final key and SSC's processing rules.

sections.title: Move from Tier 1 review to Tier 2 work
sections.body:
Classify mistakes into concept, reading, calculation and time allocation. Repair the first failed step on three fresh problems; copying a solution is not a repair. Keep the [error notebook](/study-guides/error-notebook-for-exam-preparation/) short enough to revisit.

Start the [Tier 2 guide](/exams/ssc-cgl/guides/tier-2-strategy/) alongside this review. English, maths and reasoning need deeper practice; computer knowledge and the qualifying data-entry task also need scheduled attention. If your preferred post requires an additional paper, check that requirement separately. A hoped-for Tier 1 cutoff is not a reason to postpone all next-stage study.

drills.prompt: 72 correct, 14 wrong and 14 unattempted: what is the Tier 1 raw score?
drills.explanation: 72 × 2 − 14 × 0.5 = 144 − 7. The counts add to 100. This is raw-score arithmetic, not a normalisation estimate.

drills.prompt: Two candidates have the same raw score in different shifts. Must they receive the same normalised score?
drills.answer: No exact normalised score can be inferred.
drills.explanation: Normalisation depends on the official method and the relevant score distributions. A response sheet alone does not supply that information.

checklist: Save the matching official response sheet and notice.
Reconcile correct, wrong and unanswered counts.
Write evidence for each proposed objection.
Retry three questions from my main error category.
Schedule the next Tier 2 and keyboard practice blocks.

faqs.q: What is the current CGL 2026 challenge deadline?
faqs.a: The 4 November notice gives 7 November 2026 at 9 PM IST as the closing time for online challenges and response/key viewing. The fee is ₹50 per question/answer challenged. Check SSC for any later change.

faqs.q: Does a raw score establish qualification?
faqs.a: No. Qualification comes from SSC’s published result for the matching category and post/stage rules.
